data.title: memphis/: site is clipped in the built page (1150px unreachable) — give it its own scroll container

data.body:
Review (self-review: sub-agent spawning is disabled in this session — flagging rather than claiming an independent review).

ROOT CAUSE, measured not guessed. The shell is 'html, body { height:100%; overflow:hidden }' + 'body > [data-site] { height:100% }'. memphis/style.css set only 'overflow-x: clip' on html,body and never claimed a scroll container. 'clip' + 'visible' is a LEGAL computed pair — unlike 'hidden' + 'visible' it does not force the other axis to 'auto' — so the wrapper computed overflow-y: visible, the surplus 1150px of a 1863px page overflowed, and the shell's body overflow:hidden discarded it. 62% of the page unreachable. Standalone scrolled fine, so it was a build-only divergence and invisible without measuring.

FIX. Two lines on memphis's existing body rule (height:100%, overflow-y:auto), copying isomorphic/style.css:39-48, which is the reference implementation and already carries a comment explaining the pattern. build.js untouched: the shell contract is documented in CLAUDE.md and nine other sites are written to it.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION (headless Chrome, computed styles + scripted scroll):
- Built page 1450x800: #site-memphis overflow-y auto, scrollTop reaches max 1150, atBottom true. Screenshot of the scrolled-to-bottom state shows the GitHub/Twitter/Email cards, the 'Cheap materials, taken seriously.' band and the 'Milan, 1981' footer — all previously unreachable.
- No horizontal scroll: docScrollWidth == docClientWidth == 1450, wrapperScrollWidth == wrapperClientWidth. The document itself still does not scroll.
- Standalone /memphis/ unchanged: body used height computes to 1862.78px (height:100% resolves to auto against an auto-height html, exactly as predicted, so overflow-y:auto never engages), docScrollHeight 1863, page scrolls, no h-scroll. Same content height as before the change.
- Re-swept all ten desktop buckets at 800px tall before and after. Only memphis changed: CLIPPED 1150px -> no. Every other site's numbers are byte-identical.

DISCOVERED, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: random shows 178px of wrapper overflow at 850x800. Checked standalone — html { overflow:hidden; position:fixed } means it does not scroll there either (docScrollHeight == docClientHeight == 713, pageScrolls false). Built and standalone behave identically, so it is a design choice of the original site, not a build regression. Left alone.

PROCESS NOTE: one 'node build.js' run crashed mid-session (stack trace, no output file), so an intermediate verification sweep silently measured a stale index.html and appeared to show the fix had not worked. Re-running built clean and the sweep then showed the fix. Worth knowing that a failed build leaves the previous index.html in place, so a verification pass can read stale output — always confirm the build line printed before trusting a measurement.

Scope: memphis/style.css and the rebuilt root index.html only.

Meets acceptance criteria.
